links.outcome: Change in ChatGPT mental health responses when patient LGBTQIA+ or straight identity is disclosed
links.effect: Identity disclosure did not substantially affect completeness or supportive guidance. LGBTQIA+ responses had substantially more identity acknowledgment, contextual expansion, unsupported assumptions and occasional stereotypical reasoning than the other two conditions.
links.quote: Our findings indicate that LGBTQIA+ identity disclosure did not substantially affect response completeness or supportive guidance.

links.outcome: Stereotypical reasoning and unsupported assumptions in responses to LGBTQIA+-identified users
links.effect: LGBTQIA+-explicit responses showed substantially more unsupported assumptions and occasional stereotypical reasoning than the no-disclosure and straight-disclosure conditions.
links.quote: However, responses in the LGBTQIA+-explicit condition presented substantially more identity acknowledgment, contextual expansion, unsupported assumptions, and occasional stereotypical reasoning compared to both other conditions.

screen.reason: Evaluates bias/fairness of an LLM responding to mental health questions across different demographic/identity disclosures without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
